characters.name: Peter Parker
characters.summary: The shy, noble Peter Parker bitten by a genetically-enhanced spider in the Raimi trilogy. He fought the Green Goblin, Doctor Octopus and Venom, and crossed into the MCU during the multiversal breach of No Way Home, where he reunited with his alternate-universe counterparts.
source_notes: The first big-screen Spider-Man; returns as a variant in Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021).

characters.name: Mary Jane Watson
characters.summary: Peter Parker's lifelong love, an aspiring actress who runs between superhero tragedy and her own ambitions. She finally married Peter before the multiversal breach.
source_notes: Peter's on-again, off-again partner across the Raimi trilogy.

characters.name: Norman Osborn
characters.summary: The brilliant, ruthless founder of Oscorp who split into a murderous Green Goblin persona after his experimental serum. He died at his own glider in 2002, but a variant crossed over in No Way Home and fatally wounded Aunt May.
source_notes: Killed by his own glider in Spider-Man (2002); returns as a variant in No Way Home.

characters.name: Otto Octavius
characters.summary: A brilliant physicist whose fusion experiment fused four mechanical tentacles to his spine and corrupted his mind. He drowned saving the city, but a pre-corruption variant was pulled into the MCU in No Way Home.
source_notes: Redemptive antagonist of Spider-Man 2 (2004); variant appears in No Way Home.

characters.name: Harry Osborn
characters.summary: Peter's best friend and Norman Osborn's son, who inherited the Goblin mantle believing Spider-Man killed his father. He discovered Peter's identity, saved him from Venom, and died from his injuries after reconciling.
source_notes: Becomes the New Goblin in Spider-Man 3 (2007).

characters.name: Flint Marko
characters.summary: A desperate fugitive transformed into living sand by a particle accelerator. He was revealed to be the true killer of Uncle Ben, but chose redemption alongside Spider-Man against Venom.
source_notes: Tragic figure who accidentally killed Uncle Ben; turns ally against Venom.

characters.name: Eddie Brock
characters.summary: A rival photographer who bonded with the black alien symbiote that had briefly corrupted Spider-Man. The union created the monstrous Venom, who teamed with Sandman before being destroyed along with the symbiote.
source_notes: The Raimi-universe Venom, separate from the Tom Hardy version.

characters.name: Gwen Stacy
characters.summary: A scientist's daughter and a brief love rival to Mary Jane in Spider-Man 3, whom Venom targeted to hurt Spider-Man.
source_notes: Minor role in Spider-Man 3; distinct from the Webb-universe Gwen.

characters.name: May Parker
characters.summary: Peter's warm, principled aunt who raised him after his parents died and nearly died of illness until Peter used his power to save her. She married again and survived into the No Way Home era.
source_notes: A stabilizing moral influence on Peter across the trilogy.

characters.name: Ben Parker
characters.summary: Peter's gentle uncle whose murder imparted the lesson that 'with great power there must also come great responsibility.' He was shot by the fleeing Flint Marko.
characters.image_alt: 04/01/11 Cardiff V Leeds, Championship, Cardiff City Stadium, Cardiff, Wales
source_notes: His death motivates Peter to become Spider-Man.

characters.name: J. Jonah Jameson
characters.summary: The blustery, anti-spider crusading editor of the Daily Bugle who pays Peter for photos of Spider-Man. The same J.K. Simmons incarnation later headlines the MCU's YouTube-style bugle in Far From Home.
source_notes: A variant played by J.K. Simmons appears in the MCU (Far From Home onward).

characters.name: Peter Parker
characters.summary: The quip-heavy, skateboarding Peter Parker of the Webb duology, orphaned and seeking the truth about his parents. He lost Gwen Stacy and blamed himself, then redeemed himself by saving Michelle in No Way Home.
source_notes: Returns for redemption arc in Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021).

characters.name: Gwen Stacy
characters.summary: A brilliant Oscorp scientist and Peter's girlfriend, whose death - snapped by the Green Goblin - became the defining tragedy of the Webb films and Peter's deepest regret.
source_notes: Her death in The Amazing Spider-Man 2 haunts the Garfield version.

characters.name: Dr. Curt Connors
characters.summary: A one-armed OsCorp geneticist who regrew his arm with a lizard-based serum but devolved into a monstrous, feral Lizard bent on 'rebuilding' humanity. He was cured, then pulled into No Way Home's multiversal breach.
source_notes: Appears in No Way Home as a variant.

characters.name: Max Dillon
characters.summary: An overlooked Oscorp electrical engineer who transformed into a being of pure electrical power after an accident, resenting the world and Spider-Man. A variant returned energy-starved in No Way Home.
source_notes: Appears in No Way Home, seeking the Arc Reactor.

characters.name: Harry Osborn
characters.summary: The embittered son of Norman Osborn who blamed Peter for his father's death. He experimented on himself, becoming the Goblin and killing Gwen Stacy before dying of his injuries.
source_notes: Responsible for Gwen Stacy's death.

characters.name: Aleksei Sytsevich
characters.summary: A Russian gangster who dons a towering mechanized rhino suit. He rampaged through Manhattan in the film's cliffhanger ending, brawling with Spider-Man as sirens blared.
source_notes: Final battle set-up that was never followed up due to the franchise's reboot.

characters.name: George Stacy
characters.summary: Gwen's protective father and an NYPD captain who investigated Spider-Man, learning his identity only after being fatally wounded saving him from the Lizard. He made Peter promise to stay away from Gwen.
source_notes: His dying request sets up the tragedy with Gwen.

characters.name: May Parker
characters.summary: The sharp-tongued but loving aunt who raised Peter with her late husband Ben, eventually learning and accepting that Peter is Spider-Man.
source_notes: A more independent, knowing Aunt May than the Raimi version.

characters.name: Eddie Brock
characters.summary: A freelance investigative journalist who bonded with an alien symbiote named Venom, becoming a violent anti-hero 'lethal protector' of San Francisco. A variant of him was briefly pulled into the MCU and left a piece of the symbiote behind.
source_notes: Eddie and the Venom symbiote share one body; a variant appears in No Way Home's mid-credits scene.

characters.name: Venom
characters.summary: The chaotic, hungry alien symbiote bonded to Eddie Brock. It speaks its own thoughts, feeds on chocolates and host brains, and left a fragment in the MCU when a variant was pulled through at the end of No Way Home.
source_notes: A surviving droplet of the symbiote remains in the MCU.

characters.name: Cletus Kasady
characters.summary: A serial killer and Eddie's estranged childhood acquaintance who bonded with the offspring of the Venom symbiote, becoming the sadistic red monster Carnage. He was destroyed alongside his symbiote.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of Venom: Let There Be Carnage.

characters.name: Frances Barrison
characters.summary: A pyrokinetic prisoner with a sonic scream who becomes Cletus Kasady's love interest and ally, unleashing chaos while Carnage battles Venom.
source_notes: Pairs with Carnage in Let There Be Carnage.

characters.name: Anne Weying
characters.summary: Eddie Brock's ex-fiancée and close friend, a lawyer who briefly bonded with the Venom symbiote to save a hostage and who continues to defend Eddie through the symbiote saga.
characters.image_alt: Interior artwork from The Amazing Spider-Man vol. 1, 375 (March 1993 Marvel Comics) Art by Mark Magley
source_notes: Bonds with the symbiote to fight in Venom (2018).

characters.name: Dr. Michael Morbius
characters.summary: A brilliant Nobel-winning biologist with a rare blood disease who transformed himself with bat DNA, gaining vampiric powers and a thirst for blood. He wages war on his former friend Milo and the vampire he became.
source_notes: The Living Vampire of the SSU; frog-meme beloved in pop culture.

characters.name: Lucien Crown
characters.summary: Michael Morbius's wealthy childhood friend who shared the same blood disease. After injecting himself with the same bat serum, he embraced his monstrous vampirism before being destroyed by Morbius.
source_notes: The antagonist of Morbius (2022).

characters.name: Sergei Kravinoff
characters.summary: A Russian aristocrat whose near-death encounter with a lion granted him enhanced strength and an animal connection. He hunts the villains who threaten his family, refusing to use guns against his prey.
source_notes: The SSU's anti-hero take on the classic Spider-Man villain.

characters.name: Calypso Ezili
characters.summary: A forensic psychiatrist who aids Sergei Kravinoff and is drawn into his violent family affairs, serving as his confidante.
source_notes: Comic counterpart is the voodoo priestess Calypso.

characters.name: Nikolai Kravinoff
characters.summary: Sergei's ambitious half-brother who experiments on himself with a rhinoceros serum, transforming into a monstrous human-rhino hybrid hunting his brother for control of the family empire.
source_notes: A separate, animal-berserker Rhino from the Webb-universe version.

characters.name: Unknown / The Foreigner
characters.summary: A lethal assassin hired to kill a Mobster whom Kraven protects. His fatal encounter with one of Kraven's animal allies sets off the film's violent chain of events.
characters.image_alt: King Abdulaziz with a Foreigner in the 1930s
source_notes: Classic Spider-Man mercenary adapted for the SSU.

characters.name: Aleksei Ribery
characters.summary: Kraven's ruthless father, a powerful crime lord who hunted exotic animals for sport and sought to expand his empire, ultimately meeting his end at the hands of his own sons.
source_notes: The villainous family patriarch of Kraven the Hunter.

characters.name: Cassandra Webb
characters.summary: A New York paramedic who begins seeing fragmented visions of the future after a near-fatal incident, learning to guide the young women who will become the Spider-Women against the hunter Ezekiel Sims.
source_notes: The SSU's clairvoyant hero; connects the Spider-Girls.

characters.name: Ezekiel Sims
characters.summary: A wealthy industrialist who gained spider powers in the Peruvian Amazon and used his future-visions to hunt down the young women destined to become the Spider-Women before they can appear.
source_notes: Antagonist of Madame Web; spider-powers mirroring the Spider-People.

characters.name: Julia Cornwall
characters.summary: A teenage New Yorker with a flair for impulsive decisions, one of three friends who discover spider abilities as Madame Web guides them away from Ezekiel Sims.
source_notes: Comic counterpart becomes Spider-Woman (Julia Carpenter).

characters.name: Anya Corazon
characters.summary: A whip-smart and determined Brooklyn teen, one of the three future spider-heroes protected by Cassandra Webb as they awake to their powers.
source_notes: Adaptation of Anya Corazon, the comics' Spider-Girl.

characters.name: Mattie Franklin
characters.summary: An outspoken, rebellious teenager and loyal friend, one of the three girls fated to become spider-powered heroes whose paths are guided by Madame Web away from Ezekiel Sims.
characters.image_alt: Mattie Washburn House at 8660 Franklin Street, Windsor, California.  View looking northeast.
source_notes: Comics' Mattie Franklin was one of several Spider-Women.
